Core.name: The Core
Core.environment: Fleet Academy, Admiralty, research halls, mature infrastructure and disciplined transit instrumentation in blue, gold, white and polished technical materials.
Core.tone: Institutional confidence tempered by the responsibility of maintaining systems other worlds depend on.
Core.political: Crown and Fleet authority is strongest here, but this story treats that authority as infrastructure stewardship with real structural power rather than automatic ownership of civilian life.

Corridors.name: The Public Corridor Network
Corridors.environment: Three-dimensional certified low-tension volumes centered on surveyed beacon spines. The usable cross-section is approximately circular rather than a port/starboard channel, and traffic stays near the measured direct path from one verified beacon to the next.
Corridors.tone: Routine public movement built on invisible physics and continuous measurement.
Corridors.political: The network is a public utility and a strategic power base. Whoever can certify, maintain, close, reopen or bypass routes can affect trade, relief, military logistics and political legitimacy.

Lattice.name: Lattice margins / unsurveyed space
Lattice.environment: Space outside the mature green network where reciprocal-field tension, gradients, shear and phase must be measured directly rather than assumed from public charts.
Lattice.tone: Scientific awe, patience and objective risk; never mystical.
Lattice.political: Survey knowledge becomes power because a usable route may connect people the public map leaves isolated or allow movement beyond Fleet observation.

Verge.name: The Verge
Verge.environment: Working ports, farms, markets, local stations and civilian ships whose green route boards determine what can arrive and leave.
Verge.tone: Ordinary life made possible or impossible by distant technical decisions.
Verge.political: Verge dependence gives the public green network its moral purpose while also making Fleet control of that network politically consequential.
